newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Coal & Allied strike may last two weeks.
newsitem.headline: Coal & Allied strike may last two weeks.

text.p: Coal & Allied Industries Ltd said on Wednesday the strike at its Hunter Valley Number One coal mine could last two weeks or even longer and that it may struggle to meet contracts if it lasts longer than two weeks.
"The indication from the unions is that they'll try and strike for two weeks," said Allan Davies, the general manager of operations at the mine, north of Sydney.
Davies told Reuters the company had applied for an Australian Industrial Commission ruling that would make the strike illegal, but did not expect a ruling until late Thursday.
"If the strike is protracted for longer than two weeks, it may well be difficult for us to meet some of our contractual requirements," Davies said.
Coal and Allied, 71 percent owned by Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd, expects the strike to cost A$1 million a day in lost revenue.
The mine usually produces up to 7.5 million tonnes of coal a year, mainly for power utilities in Japan and East Asia.
The union has organised the strike in protest against the company's accommodation of some workers requests for alternative employment arrangements, Davies said.
The union has refused to continue negotiations on an enterprise bargain at the mine until Coal and Allied stops offering the alternative employment arrangements.
Davies said the company was committed to improving productivity at the mine, which has a cpital value of A$430 million and employs 550 workers.
Coal and Allied shares were untraded at 1.45 p.m. (0345 GMT). The stock closed at A$9.25 on Tuesday, down 15 cents.
